Review fixes: a template is drawn as its frame says; a running elapsed clock says when it turns (rich-animation-27tq.wrw)

TemplateFrame carries reducedMotion and asciiOnly beside time and onHold,
and templateFrame(options) reads one off render options; registration
keeps only the timeline. animationFuncs reads its frame once a call.
TimeElapsedColumn places a per-second clock, so an App repaints it.
rich-dash steps on one timer gated by the app's phase; the lifecycle demo
makes only the lines not yet gone.

A view that moves says so only through what it draws (rich-animation-27tq.wrw)

A view is a renderable or a function asked for one each frame and handed no
time; a host holds one shape and draws it one way. App.animate(),
WidgetApp.animate(), the animations set, FrameSays.held and Task.time are
gone: the frame's holds alone decide whether a host ticks.

Animation.time() is the time itself, reduced to itself, so a clock or a
counter keeps the time under reduced motion. animationFuncs takes a
TemplateFrame ({ time, onHold }) and tween, loop and stepped tell their
hold, so a template in an App paints while a tween moves and sleeps after.

rich-dash steps its widgets as program state on its own timer; effects-feel,
lifecycle and the animation playground place their time-dependent parts.

A colour transition draws a time the same whatever was drawn before (rich-animation-27tq.ws0) (#513)

* A colour transition's frame is worked out from its time and cells alone (rich-animation-27tq.ws0)

ownChange kept each cell's change in a closure Map, settled in the first
frame that listed it, so a seek, reverse or scrub over an element whose
cells changed drew a later frame's settlement for an earlier time, and one
transition on two elements shared one record keyed by row:col. The record
and order()'s place cache are gone; each frame spreads its cells over the
order it lists. Cost, kept on purpose: a cell of an element that grows mid
transition may move its start.

* A cell's change is a value for its frame; the growing-element trade-off is said where it shows (rich-animation-27tq.ws0)

A frame's hold no cell carries is told, not drawn (rich-animation-27tq.5j9) (#512)

* A frame's hold no cell carries is told, not drawn (rich-animation-27tq.5j9)

A placed animation showing nothing led its output with Segment.carrier, and
a container that cut it into rows grew a blank row for it. No segment rule
can fix that: a child of no cells is zero rows, with nothing left to carry
the hold through. RenderOptions.onHold carries it instead, back the way the
frame's time came in, so any container that hands a child its options hands
back its hold. Segment.carrier, isCarrier, splitRows and Tree's carriers go.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* A held or measured animation still tells its hold (rich-animation-27tq.5j9)

holding() and measuring() dropped onHold, so a toast not yet entered in a
fitted Panel or a header-less Table column (sized to its 0-cell measure,
drawn held) told the host nothing and the frame never woke. onHold now
reaches wherever the frame's time does; placedMeasure tells its hold too.
Scroll's one-column draw, kept only to carry a hold, goes. Review of PR #512.

* Say what a hold told from no width costs (rich-animation-27tq.5j9)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

An animation is drawn one way: placed (rich-animation-27tq.0tc) (#503)

* An animation is drawn one way: placed (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

Removes every public way to draw an animation at a time the caller names:
frameAt and its Stamped renderable, the Frames class, Spinner.drawnAt, and
ProgressBar's pulse: { t }, now pulse: true. A FrameSequence, a Spinner and a
pulse are placed and draw at the frame's time.

Progress draws its table in a frame of its own host's time when printed with
none, so the bars and spinners placed in it draw at the moment its tasks are
drawn at. Examples and docs place their animations; docs that played an effect
over frames at sampled moments now play it in a live fence.

* Review: the pulse test reads what Progress draws; one clock in the showcase (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

The BarColumn pulse test supplied its own frame and compared against a
literal 7.5; it now prints the Progress and compares each row to the bar
drawn in a frame for 7.5s. A test pins that, in a frame of its own host,
a Progress holds what it would draw. Spinner's placed renderable is built
in the constructor after the sequences it closes over. The showcase draws
the dashboard at the Live's frame time, so the heading and the jobs share
one clock. Two doc sentences that described examples no longer present
are corrected.

* Review: the template frames test names FrameSequence, not the removed Frames (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

* Rebase onto the escape: Spinner measures through protocol, held covers a pulsing bar (rich-animation-27tq.0tc)

A held renderable is now drawn through render (#510), so the frame a printed
Progress makes reaches what it holds as it reaches what it draws; _framed
stays as the one moment a print is drawn for.
